live verb

have one’s home

also dwell, reside, inhabit, where do you live?, live together

classical

Ter. Eun. 107: ea habitābat Rhodī
Cic. Cael. 17: in aediculīs habitat (Lewis & Short)

habitō, habitāre, habitāvī, habitātum

verb, first conjugation

live, dwell

Where one lives goes in the locative (Rhodī, Rōmae, rūrī) or with in and the ablative; with whom, cum or apud (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • vīvō, vīvere, vīxī, vīctum — live (somewhere, in some way)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 14.20.4: vīvit habitatque cum Balbō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 340

    Of the life one leads in a place: Rhodī vīvere (Cic. Fam. 4.7.4, Lewis & Short).

  • incolō, incolere, incoluī — inhabit (a land, a region)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.1.1: quārum ūnam incolunt Belgae

    Of a people and its country; in Cicero always with an accusative (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Samia mihi māter fuit: ea habitābat Rhodī.

    My mother came from Samos; she lived on Rhodes.Ter. Eun. 107

  • Ubi habitat? — Nē id quidem. — Ubi vīdistī? — In viā.

    Where does she live? — I don’t even know that. — Where did you see her? — In the street.Ter. Eun. 322

  • nōs enim ita philologī sumus ut vel cum fabrīs habitāre possīmus

    for we are such scholars that we could even live with the builders in the houseCic. Q. fr. 2.8.3

See also live, house, neighbour, village.
